llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C is represented as solid L-ascorbic acid, molecular weight 176.12 g/mol, and is separately identified as the electrochemical analyte rather than as an electrolyte component. It is added directly to the KCl electrolyte in the experiment vial before mixing. The solution should be prepared immediately before analysis because ascorbic acid can oxidize during prolonged exposure to air and light.
assumptions: A Quantos cartridge containing potassium chloride and a separate Quantos cartridge containing L-ascorbic acid are physically loaded and available at positions 1 and 2, respectively.
Water is available as a pump-compatible liquid on syringe-pump channel 1.
The stated molecular weight of Vitamin C refers to anhydrous L-ascorbic acid, C6H8O6, with molecular weight 176.12 g/mol.
The stated molecular weight of potassium chloride is 74.5513 g/mol.
The platform's pH measurement, nitrogen purge, electrode polishing, washing, drying, and stir-bar mixing operations are available as specified in the system capabilities.
The 7.000 mL dispensed water volume is treated as the final preparation volume; dissolved-solid volume is neglected for concentration calculations.
The solution is measured promptly after preparation and protected from unnecessary light and air exposure.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Required KCl moles = 0.100 mol/L x 0.007000 L = 0.000700 mol. Theoretical KCl mass = 0.000700 mol x 74.5513 g/mol = 0.05218591 g = 52.18591 mg. The planned Quantos mass is 52.185 mg. Actual KCl concentration = (0.052185 g / 74.5513 g/mol) / 0.007000 L = 0.0999983 mol/L.

Required Vitamin C moles = 0.001000 mol/L x 0.007000 L = 0.000007000 mol. Theoretical L-ascorbic acid mass = 0.000007000 mol x 176.12 g/mol = 0.00123284 g = 1.23284 mg. The planned Quantos mass is 1.233 mg. Actual Vitamin C concentration = (0.001233 g / 176.12 g/mol) / 0.007000 L = 0.00100013 mol/L.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: The plan uses 2 solid cartridges, below the maximum of 8, and 1 liquid pump channel, below the maximum of 4. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg Quantos cartridge capacity. The 7.000 mL water volume is exactly compatible with the 7 uL pump increment because 7000 uL equals 1000 dispensing increments. Final liquid volume is 7.000 mL, below the 10 mL vial limit. One electrochemical slot is used, below the maximum of 3. All solids are assigned to Quantos cartridges and water is the only pump-dispensed liquid. The electrode configuration exactly matches the available gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No analyte film is deposited and no drying step for a deposited sample is required. The gold working electrode is washed and dried as part of routine pre-measurement electrode preparation after polishing.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is performed because the requested experiment requires Vitamin C dissolved in the electrolyte. The gold working electrode is polished, washed, dried, and immersed in the prepared analyte-containing electrolyte for measurement.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 52.185 mg potassium chloride from Quantos cartridge position 1 into one clean experiment vial. Dispense 7.000 mL water from liquid pump channel 1. Add 1.233 mg L-ascorbic acid from Quantos cartridge position 2 to the same vial. Mix with a clean stir bar for 300 seconds to dissolve both solids fully. The substation then performs nitrogen purging for 300 seconds and measures electrolyte pH before the CV test.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.100 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte provides ionic conductivity while using a solid salt explicitly compatible with Quantos dispensing. A 1.00 mM Vitamin C concentration provides a measurable oxidation response without requiring excessive analyte mass. The -0.10 V to +0.70 V versus Ag/AgCl window targets the expected anodic oxidation of ascorbic acid on gold while limiting unnecessary excursion to strongly positive potentials. A 0.050 V/s scan rate, 2 mV step size, and three cycles provide a practical initial characterization and allow observation of cycle-to-cycle electrode fouling or analyte depletion. Nitrogen purging is included because dissolved oxygen can contribute reduction current and because Vitamin C is susceptible to air oxidation.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested analyte is Vitamin C dissolved directly in the electrolyte, so analite_in_electrolite mode is required. Both potassium chloride supporting electrolyte and solid L-ascorbic acid are dispensed into an experiment vial with water, mixed to homogeneity, purged with nitrogen, and measured in the electrochemical substation.

metadata.description: Characterization of dissolved L-ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) by cyclic voltammetry using a gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode in freshly prepared aqueous 0.100 M KCl supporting electrolyte.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic Voltammetry of Vitamin C in 0.100 M KCl
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize Vitamin C as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The Vitamin C should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, Vitamin C concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform.

cross_contamination_risks: Ascorbic acid oxidation products can adsorb on the gold working electrode and alter subsequent voltammograms; wash and dry the electrode after the measurement.
Residual chloride electrolyte in the electrochemical cell or on electrodes can contaminate subsequent low-chloride experiments.
Use dedicated or thoroughly cleaned stir bars and experiment vials to prevent carryover of electroactive analytes.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, nitrile gloves, and safety glasses when loading solid cartridges and handling solutions.
Avoid inhalation of potassium chloride and Vitamin C powder during cartridge loading.
Use freshly prepared Vitamin C solution and begin the nitrogen purge and CV measurement promptly to minimize air oxidation of ascorbic acid.
Polish, wash, and dry the gold working electrode before measurement to remove residues from prior experiments.
Confirm the Ag/AgCl reference electrode is intact, filled appropriately, and not allowed to dry out.
hazards: L-ascorbic acid is a low-hazard organic acid but may cause eye irritation or irritation from dust exposure.
Potassium chloride is low hazard but solid dust should not be inhaled or introduced into eyes.
The prepared Vitamin C solution is mildly acidic and should be handled as an aqueous chemical solution.
Electrode polishing and electrochemical operation present contamination and splash risks.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV aqueous potassium chloride and Vitamin C solution in the designated aqueous non-heavy-metal electrochemical waste container, unless local waste procedures require a different stream.
Dispose of electrode polishing residues and wipes according to the laboratory procedure for electrode-maintenance waste.
Do not return used electrolyte or rinse liquid to reagent reservoirs.
